sanity_expectations: At t=0, dq/dt = i = 0 exactly, di/dt is negative and finite, resistance initially relaxes negligibly because Joule heating starts at zero current, and capacitance decreases rapidly from its inherited initial value 1.0 toward a much smaller charge-dependent target near small_signal_capacitance.

Because the capacitor restoring term is divided by 1 + capacitance_relaxation_time*|i|/sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance), segments with larger |i| should show weaker instantaneous q-driven restoring action than matched low-|i| segments at similar q and capacitance; this effect is strongest away from current zero crossings.

When |i| approaches a noticeable fraction of saturation_current_scale = 0.08 A, the effective inductive denominator decreases, so |di/dt| should increase relative to a constant-inductance baseline mainly during higher-current portions, not uniformly over the whole trajectory.

Resistance should remain positive and drift only moderately upward over the window; any thermal change should lag electrical oscillation because the thermal state evolves on a slower timescale than the LC motion.

Field-dependent capacitance enhancement is limited to order-one changes around |q| comparable to capacitance_field_scale = 0.001, but the inherited nonequilibrium initial capacitance state is much larger and therefore early-time capacitance behavior is dominated by relaxation from the imposed initial condition rather than by the field-dependent target alone.
role_corrections: di_dt: claimed-output/target derivative -> derivative label only, not dependent variable (overridden: in the typed ODE system the dependent variable is target_state i, while di_dt is the RHS-defined time derivative)
q: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state variable (confirmed)
i: claimed-dynamic state -> dependent variable and dynamic state variable (confirmed)
resistance: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state variable (confirmed by explicit state equation and preserved per freedom_change none)
capacitance: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state variable (confirmed by explicit state equation and preserved per freedom_change none)
rationale: The typed ODE contract is preserved exactly as required: the sampled axis is time only, dependent variable is the target state i, and the full four-state system is inherited without reordering. The chosen parameters keep the dynamics passive and finite while making the intended refinements observable from the inherited initial release q(0)=0.001, i(0)=0. With inductance*small_signal_capacitance = 5e-4, the small-signal LC timescale is sqrt(LC) ≈ 0.022 s, so the time window 0 to 0.25 s spans about 11 small-signal oscillation times and should show several ring-down cycles before strong flattening. The saturation current scale 0.08 A is neither unreachable nor deep in saturation: from the initial stored energy q0^2/(2C0)=5e-7 J and L=0.5 H, a linear estimate gives peak current around q0/sqrt(LC0) ≈ 0.045 A, so trajectories should probe a moderate fraction of saturation_current_scale rather than remaining fully linear or fully saturated. The dielectric lag factor uses capacitance_relaxation_time/sqrt(LC_small) ≈ 1.34, meaning current-dependent weakening of the capacitor restoring term can be noticeable when |i| is appreciable, especially early in the discharge, but it vanishes automatically near current zero crossings. The capacitance state is initialized at 1.0 while its small-signal target is 0.001, so the capacitance relaxation dynamics will dominate immediately; this inherited initial state is physically extreme and supersedes subtle field-dependent capacitance modulation at the earliest times, but it must be preserved. The chosen capacitance_relaxation_time keeps that inherited transient observable rather than numerically instantaneous. Thermal evolution is set slower than the electrical motion: thermal_capacity=8 and thermal_resistance_gain=0.6 with heating_saturation_power=0.02 make resistance drift moderate over the 0.25 s window rather than frozen or explosively fast, so history-dependent damping can emerge later in the ring-down if Joule power becomes appreciable. Because the inherited initial capacitance is far above small_signal_capacitance, early motion may be slower and less oscillatory than a near-equilibrium capacitor start; this is an honest limitation of the given contract, not repaired here. No observation noise is added.

scenario_text: A series circuit containing an inductor, resistor, and capacitor is released from a charged initial state. The circuit current and capacitor charge exchange energy through the electric and magnetic storage elements while resistance removes energy. The baseline model uses fixed component values and excludes external driving after release.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt is affine in the observed states (q,i) with one fixed damping coefficient resistance/inductance, so for a shared parameter set the decay envelope and oscillation frequency are fixed by the same constant resistance across the whole release trajectory.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same state dependence but relax fixed linear damping by letting effective resistance increase with current magnitude, so di_dt gains a state-dependent damping interaction between i and the resistive term.
response_change.observable_effect: Larger-current portions of the ring-down are damped more strongly than later small-current portions, producing amplitude-dependent envelope curvature and stronger early-cycle suppression that the parent's single constant resistance cannot match simultaneously.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the release produces currents large enough that self-heating or other current-dependent dissipation changes the effective resistance over the observed transient; negligible-current ring-down should recover the parent behavior.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, early high-|i| segments already show stronger damping than late low-|i| segments at the same fixed component values; in holdout with larger initial energy this same amplitude-dependent damping becomes more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing current-dependent resistance correction, or over trajectories confined to sufficiently small |i|, the model reduces continuously to the parent linear RLC law.
plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes dissipation is strictly linear and time-invariant, omitting amplitude-dependent effective resistance during a finite-energy discharge.
plan.baseline_assumption: The components are linear and time-invariant, specifically that resistance is a fixed constant independent of current amplitude during the release.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Current-dependent resistive dissipation, such as heating-induced increase of effective resistance during higher-current portions of the transient.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax fixed linear resistance rather than add an unrelated mechanism. In the parent, with inductance and capacitance held fixed, varying only the instantaneous state along the release gives a target mapping di_dt determined by one constant damping gain and one constant restoring gain. This creates a shortcut: one shared resistance sets the whole decay shape. In the child, the damping slope with respect to i changes with |i|, so early high-current portions of a trajectory can decay faster than later low-current portions even under the same nominal component values and no external drive. The concrete contrast is amplitude-dependent ring-down: for releases that reach appreciable current, peaks shrink disproportionately faster at the start, while small-amplitude segments approach the parent law. A single refitted parent resistance cannot reproduce both the weak late-time damping and the stronger early-time damping across such conditions, because increasing resistance enough to fit the initial decay would overdamp the later small-current segment, while fitting the tail would underdamp the initial peaks. This is admissible in passive unforced operation because the modification only increases dissipation and does not inject energy. The effect is limited if currents remain too small for resistance variation to matter; in that regime the parent may already be adequate.

contract.parent_reduction: Set resistance_nonlinear_coeff = 0, or restrict to trajectories with resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) << resistance.

range_suggestions.resistance_nonlinear_coeff: >= 0; small enough that low-|i| behavior remains near linear, but large enough that resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) is comparable to resistance in high-current transients

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt depends on q and i with a fixed dissipative law -(resistance + resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i))*i, so for fixed q the damping contribution is an instantaneous function of current only.
response_change.child_relation: Release the resistor's effective resistance from a fixed parameter to a slowly evolving thermal state, so di_dt depends on q, i, and the accumulated recent current history through self-heating; for the same instantaneous i and q, the slope can differ depending on prior dissipation.
response_change.observable_effect: In larger-amplitude ring-downs the late-time decay becomes more strongly damped than early-time decay because heating accumulates, whereas the parent can only tie damping instantaneously to |i| and cannot create this history-dependent curvature change with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when Joule heating integrated over several oscillation or decay times is large enough to change effective resistance appreciably, while thermal relaxation is not so fast that resistance remains effectively instantaneous; practically, moderate-to-large initial stored energy and finite ring-down duration are required.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Across trajectories with different initial charge but fixed component values, training already contains stronger dissipation for larger-amplitude releases; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to a distinct history effect: at matched instantaneous i and q reached at different times within a transient, the child predicts different di_dt because the resistor has warmed.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of negligible self-heating or infinitely fast thermal equilibration to a constant ambient value, the evolved resistance becomes effectively constant and the parent law is recovered.
plan.promotion_reason: A fixed resistance cannot encode thermal memory. To make the target mapping history dependent under the same observed q and i, the effective resistance itself must evolve as a state driven by dissipation.
plan.gap_statement: The model treats resistance as fixed apart from instantaneous current dependence, omitting resistor self-heating that changes damping over the course of the transient.
plan.baseline_assumption: The circuit is series-connected with fixed resistance, inductance, and capacitance.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Electrothermal resistance drift: Joule dissipation heats the resistor, increasing its effective resistance on a finite thermal timescale during the free decay.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-resistance assumption rather than add an unrelated new force. The parent's target mapping uses a single instantaneous damping law, so once q and i are specified, di_dt is fixed. That is a fixed-environment shortcut because the dissipative environment cannot evolve with absorbed energy. In practice, with different initial capacitor charges and all other component values held fixed, higher-energy releases dissipate more Joule power and can warm the resistor during the observed ring-down. Then the same instantaneous pair (q,i) reached later in a strong transient can produce a more negative di_dt than earlier or than in a weaker release, because the effective resistance has increased. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce this across conditions: increasing constant resistance to match late-time strong-run damping would overdamp weak runs and early-time strong-run segments, while increasing only resistance_nonlinear_coeff still leaves damping an instantaneous function of |i| and cannot distinguish equal |i| states with different thermal histories. The effect is scientifically admissible when heating is appreciable but not so extreme as to violate finite-state assumptions, and it may be weak for very small initial charge or very fast thermal relaxation.

plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-inductance assumption, not to add another dissipative channel. response_change.child_relation: Release the fixed-capacitance assumption by allowing capacitance to evolve with voltage magnitude through dielectric absorption/field-dependent permittivity, so the q-to-di_dt contribution changes with the contemporaneous charge state and creates a state-dependent interaction between q and the oscillation frequency/curvature.
response_change.observable_effect: Across free decays with different initial charge amplitudes but the same component parameter set, larger-|q| portions of the trajectory show a different local oscillation timescale and q-to-di_dt curvature than small-|q| portions; the parent can only rescale this contribution with one fixed capacitance.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when the release is strong enough that capacitor voltage is not confined to the small-signal dielectric regime, yet remains within admissible finite-energy operation; strongest at early high-|q| portions of the discharge before thermal drift fully dominates.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate releases may already show slight amplitude-dependent period or q-curvature changes; in holdout with stronger initial charge the same mechanism extends to clearer within-trajectory variation of the q-to-di_dt mapping rather than a uniform rescaling.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the small-signal dielectric limit where capacitance becomes effectively constant over the observed voltage range.
contract.promotion_reason: A genuine dielectric relaxation or voltage-dependent effective capacitance has memory on the discharge timescale; a fixed parameter cannot represent within-trajectory evolution of the q-to-voltage relation, and no existing state tracks capacitor internal polarization.
contract.domain_mechanism: dielectric relaxation with saturating field-dependent effective capacitance
contract.scientific_mechanism: Dielectric polarization relaxation or field-dependent permittivity causes the effective capacitance to evolve during the transient, changing the restoring voltage associated with a given stored charge.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the restoring coefficient on q is no longer a single fixed number; it is generated by a coupled state with finite relaxation toward a saturating charge-dependent target, producing within-trajectory memory and amplitude-dependent curvature.
contract.assumption_before: Capacitance is constant and time-invariant throughout the free discharge.
contract.assumption_after: Effective capacitance relaxes toward a saturating charge-dependent dielectric state during the transient.
contract.parent_reduction: Take capacitance_relaxation_time -> 0 with capacitance_field_gain = 0 so capacitance = small_signal_capacitance, and identify small_signal_capacitance with the parent capacitance.
contract.observable_signature: With one shared parameter set, stronger-charge releases show larger early-time effective capacitance and thus weaker instantaneous restoring voltage magnitude q/capacitance, followed by relaxation toward the small-signal regime; this appears as amplitude-dependent local period and q-curvature that diminishes later in the same trajectory.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters still leaves the target mapping's q dependence as exactly one fixed factor 1/capacitance for all times and amplitudes. That single shared scaling cannot reproduce both the early high-|q| weakened restoring action and the later low-|q| small-signal restoring action within the same trajectory or across multiple initial-charge conditions without violating the retained inductive and resistive structure.

range_suggestions.capacitance: positive; initialize near the nominal small-signal capacitance and allow moderate transient deviations under strong release
range_suggestions.capacitance_relaxation_time: > 0; comparable to or somewhat longer than the early LC oscillation timescale sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) when dielectric memory is observable
range_suggestions.small_signal_capacitance: > 0; equal to the parent capacitance in the small-signal recovery limit
range_suggestions.capacitance_field_gain: >= 0; small to order-one fractional capacitance enhancement under strong but finite charge loading
range_suggestions.capacitance_field_scale: > 0; charge scale comparable to upper-middle transient |q| where amplitude dependence first becomes visible

response_change.parent_relation: The capacitor contribution to di_dt is a single-valued restoring term -q/capacitance, so after capacitance is set by |q| the electrical restoring slope depends only on q and not on the instantaneous current direction or discharge rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the quasi-static capacitor law with a rate-sensitive capacitive back-voltage so the restoring contribution depends jointly on q and i, producing different effective electrical stiffness on charging versus discharging portions of the transient.
response_change.observable_effect: At comparable |q|, high-|i| segments show altered di_dt curvature and shifted peak-current decay relative to low-|i| segments; the parent cannot create this same-q, different-slope contrast because its capacitor voltage depends only on q/capacitance.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when capacitance_relaxation_time is comparable to or longer than the early LC timescale sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) and the release amplitude is large enough that both |q| and |i| become appreciable before the oscillation is strongly damped.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate release amplitudes already show mild mismatch between same-|q| segments with different |i|; in holdout, stronger releases amplify this rate-sensitive curvature difference without requiring a new intervention or changed initial-condition protocol.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the dielectric response to be quasi-static so the capacitor back-voltage depends only on q/capacitance and not on current-driven polarization lag.
plan.gap_statement: The current model lets capacitance relax in time but still assumes the capacitor voltage entering di_dt is instantaneously given by q/capacitance, omitting nonequilibrium dielectric back-voltage during fast polarization lag.
plan.baseline_assumption: The effective capacitor is treated as quasi-static: once capacitance(t) is known, the capacitor voltage is fully determined by q/capacitance with no additional rate-dependent polarization contribution.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's quasi-static capacitor assumption rather than adding a wholly new physical subsystem. The parent already includes dielectric relaxation through the capacitance state, but in the scored target mapping di_dt the capacitor enters only through -q/capacitance. That means two times during the transient with the same q and capacitance must produce the same electrical restoring contribution regardless of whether the capacitor is rapidly discharging or recharging. Scientifically, this is a shortcut: when dielectric polarization relaxes on a timescale comparable to the oscillation, the terminal capacitor voltage is not determined solely by q and the slowly evolving capacitance state. Vary the release amplitude so that one set of trajectories explores larger early |i| while holding the component parameters fixed. Under admissible conditions with capacitance_relaxation_time not much shorter than sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance), the child model predicts a same-q but different-di_dt contrast between fast and slow segments because polarization lag modifies the restoring voltage according to current direction and magnitude. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this across conditions: changing capacitance-field nonlinearity reshapes dependence on q, and changing inductive or resistive terms reshapes i effects globally, but the parent lacks a direct q-i interaction in the capacitor back-voltage itself. Limitation: if dielectric relaxation is extremely fast relative to the LC motion, the effect collapses and the parent remains adequate.

contract.domain_mechanism: rate-sensitive dielectric back-voltage in a relaxing capacitor
contract.scientific_mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the capacitor restoring contribution is no longer a fixed function of q once capacitance is known; its coefficient varies with current loading through a dimensionless timescale ratio, introducing a direct q-i interaction inside the scored target mapping.
contract.assumption_before: The capacitor voltage entering di_dt is instantaneously q/capacitance once the capacitance state is specified.
contract.assumption_after: The capacitor back-voltage is reduced during fast charge redistribution by dielectric polarization lag, implemented as a current-dependent coefficient on the restoring term.
contract.parent_reduction: When capacitance_relaxation_time*Abs(i)/sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) << 1, the additional current-dependent factor approaches 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
contract.observable_signature: Across trajectories generated with the same fixed parameters but different release amplitudes, compare time points with similar q and capacitance. contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters cannot create this contrast with one shared parameter set because the parent capacitor law is structurally single-phase: once q and capacitance are matched, the capacitor contribution is fixed at -q/capacitance. baseline_mechanisms: Exchange of energy between capacitor electric storage and inductor magnetic storage.
baseline_assumptions: The circuit is series-connected with fixed resistance, inductance, and capacitance.
The components are linear and time-invariant.
There is no external voltage drive after release.
Radiation and parasitic coupling are negligible.
scientific_constraints: Inductance, capacitance, and resistance are positive.
In the unforced circuit, total stored energy cannot increase.
The current and capacitor charge remain finite over the modeled interval.
refinement_agenda: Add an external time-dependent voltage source.
Change the linear inductor assumption to include magnetic saturation.
Add parasitic capacitance or leakage resistance.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt is affine in the observed states (q,i) with one fixed damping coefficient resistance/inductance, so for a shared parameter set the decay envelope and oscillation frequency are fixed by the same constant resistance across the whole release trajectory.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same state dependence but relax fixed linear damping by letting effective resistance increase with current magnitude, so di_dt gains a state-dependent damping interaction between i and the resistive term.
response_change.observable_effect: Larger-current portions of the ring-down are damped more strongly than later small-current portions, producing amplitude-dependent envelope curvature and stronger early-cycle suppression that the parent's single constant resistance cannot match simultaneously.

diagnostic_groups.role: Amplitude regime controlling whether nonlinear damping is activated

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when the release produces currents large enough that self-heating or other current-dependent dissipation changes the effective resistance over the observed transient; negligible-current ring-down should recover the parent behavior.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, early high-|i| segments already show stronger damping than late low-|i| segments at the same fixed component values; in holdout with larger initial energy this same amplitude-dependent damping becomes more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing current-dependent resistance correction, or over trajectories confined to sufficiently small |i|, the model reduces continuously to the parent linear RLC law.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: Amplitude-dependent resistive damping in an unforced series RLC discharge
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Current-dependent resistive dissipation, such as heating-induced increase of effective resistance during higher-current portions of the transient.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the damping coefficient is no longer constant: it is formed by combining resistance with resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) before multiplying by i, so the slope of di_dt with respect to i changes across the trajectory. That creates amplitude-dependent envelope curvature rather than a uniform rescaling of the parent linear decay.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The components are linear and time-invariant, specifically that resistance is a fixed constant independent of current amplitude during the release.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Effective resistance increases with current magnitude during the discharge, producing amplitude-dependent passive damping.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Set resistance_nonlinear_coeff = 0, or restrict to trajectories with resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) << resistance.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Compared at fixed inductance, capacitance, and baseline resistance, trajectories reaching larger |i| show disproportionately stronger early-cycle damping and a curved decay envelope, while late low-|i| segments revert toward the parent linear ring-down. This changes the scored target mapping di_dt itself, not merely an auxiliary state, because the damping term in the i equation now depends on both i and Abs(i).
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both regimes across these conditions because its damping is linear with one constant resistance. Refitting resistance high enough to match the stronger early decay would overdamp the later small-|i| tail and shift the whole trajectory, while fitting the late tail would underpredict the initial peak suppression. The mismatch is structural: the parent lacks the amplitude-dependent interaction term resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i)*i.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt depends on q and i with a fixed dissipative law -(resistance + resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i))*i, so for fixed q the damping contribution is an instantaneous function of current only.
response_change.child_relation: Release the resistor's effective resistance from a fixed parameter to a slowly evolving thermal state, so di_dt depends on q, i, and the accumulated recent current history through self-heating; for the same instantaneous i and q, the slope can differ depending on prior dissipation.
response_change.observable_effect: In larger-amplitude ring-downs the late-time decay becomes more strongly damped than early-time decay because heating accumulates, whereas the parent can only tie damping instantaneously to |i| and cannot create this history-dependent curvature change with one shared parameter set.

diagnostic_groups.name: electromagnetic_energy
diagnostic_groups.role: Stored circuit energy setting transient amplitude and accessible heating

diagnostic_groups.name: current_scale_ratio
diagnostic_groups.role: Measures when existing instantaneous nonlinear damping is important and helps separate it from slower thermal memory effects

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when Joule heating integrated over several oscillation or decay times is large enough to change effective resistance appreciably, while thermal relaxation is not so fast that resistance remains effectively instantaneous; practically, moderate-to-large initial stored energy and finite ring-down duration are required.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: Across trajectories with different initial charge but fixed component values, training already contains stronger dissipation for larger-amplitude releases; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to a distinct history effect: at matched instantaneous i and q reached at different times within a transient, the child predicts different di_dt because the resistor has warmed.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: In the limit of negligible self-heating or infinitely fast thermal equilibration to a constant ambient value, the evolved resistance becomes effectively constant and the parent law is recovered.
evolution_contracts.promotion_reason: A fixed resistance cannot encode thermal memory. To make the target mapping history dependent under the same observed q and i, the effective resistance itself must evolve as a state driven by dissipation.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: self-heating resistor with finite thermal response and saturated heating drive
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Electrothermal resistance drift: Joule dissipation heats the resistor, increasing its effective resistance on a finite thermal timescale during the free decay.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored mapping acquires a hidden memory coordinate through resistance dynamics, and the saturating heating term changes curvature between weak-heating and strong-heating regimes rather than merely rescaling damping.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The circuit is series-connected with fixed resistance, inductance, and capacitance.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The resistor self-heats during the transient, so its effective resistance evolves toward higher values under Joule power and relaxes toward ambient_resistance on a finite thermal timescale with saturating heating response.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: If thermal_resistance_gain -> 0, or thermal relaxation effectively holds resistance at ambient_resistance, then the successor reduces to the parent with resistance replaced by a constant ambient value.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: With fixed component parameters but different initial charge magnitudes, stronger releases show progressively increased damping later in the same ring-down; at matched instantaneous (q,i), later points on a strong transient have more negative di_dt than earlier points or weaker runs because resistance has risen thermally. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because di_dt directly uses the evolved resistance state.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this across those conditions because any constant resistance chosen to fit late-time damping in strong runs would overdamp early-time and low-energy segments, while changing resistance_nonlinear_coeff still leaves damping an instantaneous function of |i| only. The child can distinguish equal q and i with different prior dissipation histories through resistance memory, which the parent's memoryless mapping cannot absorb by global refitting.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt(q,i,resistance) uses a constant inductance, so at fixed q, i, and resistance the current acceleration scales with a single invariant denominator and only damping changes over the transient.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the fixed-inductance assumption by allowing effective inductance to decrease with current magnitude due to magnetic core saturation or flux-path nonlinearity, so di_dt gains a state-dependent denominator and the q,i to di_dt map bends with |i| even when resistance is unchanged.
response_change.observable_effect: Across releases that generate different peak |i| while holding component values fixed, the child predicts larger-magnitude early-time di_dt and a shortened high-current half-cycle at stronger releases, beyond what the parent can match with one shared parameter set that only changes damping.

diagnostic_groups.name: electric_restoring_per_inductance
diagnostic_groups.role: Baseline capacitor-driven acceleration scale before magnetic saturation correction

diagnostic_groups.name: damping_to_reactive_ratio
diagnostic_groups.role: Separates waveform changes caused mainly by damping from those caused by altered reactive inertia

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when initial stored charge is large enough that the transient reaches currents in the admissible range where magnetic saturation is no longer negligible, while thermal resistance evolution remains finite and the circuit stays bounded.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate and strong releases already show amplitude-dependent waveform bending; in holdout, stronger but still finite releases extend the same trend, with the child showing extra acceleration at high |i| while the parent only increases dissipation and cannot reproduce both the timing and decay with one shared fit.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of negligible saturation strength or over trajectories confined to sufficiently small |i| so the effective inductance is approximately constant.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: nonlinear magnetic softening of the inductor
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Current-driven magnetic saturation or nonlinear flux linkage reduces incremental inductance at larger |i| in a series RLC discharge.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the denominator of the target law, introducing amplitude-dependent reactive timescale compression rather than a uniform rescaling or extra loss term. The target mapping itself changes at fixed observed q, i, and resistance, so fitting only damping parameters cannot reproduce the same timing distortion across weak and strong releases.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The inductor is linear and time-invariant with fixed inductance over the full release amplitude range.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The inductor has current-dependent incremental inductance that decreases with |i| due to magnetic saturation or nonlinear flux linkage.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Recover the parent when saturation_current_scale -> oo, or along trajectories with Abs(i) << saturation_current_scale so the effective inductance is approximately inductance.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: When comparing low- and high-release trajectories generated by different initial capacitor charge magnitudes with all component parameters shared, the child shows stronger-magnitude di_dt and visibly compressed high-current portions once Abs(i) approaches saturation_current_scale. At matched observed q, i, and resistance values, di_dt is no longer set by a single constant inductive denominator, giving curvature in the q,i to di_dt map that the parent lacks.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot absorb this across both weak and strong releases because changing resistance terms mainly alters dissipation and envelope decay, while changing inductance uniformly rescales the whole trajectory. The child instead introduces a selective high-|i| reduction of inductive inertia, so the same parameter set must produce near-parent behavior at weak current and faster reactive motion only during strong-current segments; that state-dependent timing distortion is structurally unavailable to the parent.
